messages:
Aisha (People Ops): Quick Q — how do on-call stipends interact with 401(k) deferrals and HSA contributions, esp. if someone goes on unpaid parental leave mid-pay-period?

Context: stipend is a monthly taxable stipend (paid separate line item), team member will start unpaid leave on Apr 15 and still has an on-call stipend for Apr. They want to keep making HSA contributions and 401k deferrals on that stipend if possible. Any vendor/cutoff gotchas?

Matt (Platform Eng): short answer from our side: we expected stipends to be taxable wages, so deferrals apply if payroll marks them as wages. but curious how payroll should code it so vendor picks it up. also: will it break leave/unpaid logic?

Julia (Payroll): good questions. TL;DR: On-call stipend treated as eligible compensation for 401(k) deferral when coded as taxable wages (not a reimbursement). HSA pre-tax payroll contributions stop once payroll records pay as "unpaid" for the pay period; personal contributions are still possible but handled outside payroll.

Julia (Payroll): More details / steps for this case: 
- Payroll code: use ONCALL_STIP (taxable earnings).
- Mark deferral: if the employee has a %/dollar 401k election on file, our payroll engine will apply it to ONCALL_STIP by default. If they want a different election JUST for the stipend, they need to submit a manual payroll change ticket before cutoff.
- Vendor cutoff: send to Benefits vendor by payroll cutoff (we usually push 401(k) deferral file to the recordkeeper 3 business days after pay date; to affect deferrals, payroll changes must be in our system at least 2 business days before pay date).

Julia (Payroll): Example timeline: pay date Apr 20, employee goes unpaid Apr 15. To have the stipend deferred into 401(k): 
- Submit election/change by Apr 16 payroll cutoff (we recommend Apr 14 to be safe).
- We run payroll and tag ONCALL_STIP as taxable — deferral will flow to the 401(k) export.

Aisha (People Ops): If payroll stops HSA pre-tax contributions during unpaid leave, what are the employee options to keep funding the HSA?

Julia (Payroll): Options: 
- Continue HSA pre-tax via payroll only if there are taxable wages in the period (i.e., the stipend is coded as pre-tax-eligible per above). If there are no wages for the pay period, payroll cannot make pre-tax HSA deductions.
- Employee can make post-tax personal contributions directly to their HSA outside payroll and then claim the deduction on their tax return (Form 8889).
- Another option: set up a one-off payroll pre-tax deduction on the stipend if the stipend occurs in a pay period where payroll processes taxable wages — requires a manual ticket before cutoff.

Matt (Platform Eng): ok that helps. Are there any limits where recordkeeper rejects small isolated contributions from stipends? like if it's a $50 stipend, will it still show up?

Julia (Payroll): Most recordkeepers will accept small amounts, but two caveats: 
1) Minimum contribution rules — check the plan doc; historically our plan accepts any positive deferral but a few partner plans had $25 minimum.
2) Frequency rules — if someone only ever defers on a single stipend and not on regular pay, it still flows but may look odd on reports. If the employee cares about vesting/loan payments tied to payroll cadence we should review. If you want, I can ping the recordkeeper to confirm for this exact plan.

Aisha (People Ops): please ping them for confirmation (employee prefers to keep deferring $100/mo from stipend). Also, can we document the manual steps in the benefits KB?

Benefits Bot: Auto-note: benefits.plan.external-recordkeeper.link/401k-plan-docs added to thread (internal doc permissions apply).

Julia (Payroll): I will: 1) confirm min contribution/acceptance with recordkeeper, 2) add short KB snippet for "Deferring one-off stipends and leave interactions" with the timeline and the payroll codes. Tagging @Aisha for any wording preferences.

Aisha (People Ops): perfect — thanks Julia! :thumbsup:

Matt (Platform Eng): thanks all — useful to know the cutoff windows too.

(End of thread)
